summary: newtun CLI opens remote-controlled shell, file, and command channels to hardcoded server
details: The newtun CLI connects a WebSocket to the hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999 (default when -H is not supplied) and hands the remote party interactive control of the host. On TERM_OPEN the client spawns an OS shell via node-pty and pipes TERM_INPUT bytes straight into the PTY, giving the server a full interactive shell as the invoking user. SCRIPT_LIST and POLICY_SCRIPTS messages cause the client to run child_process.exec on server-supplied script content and return stdout/stderr/exitCode. FILE_REQUEST messages drive fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync/rmSync/renameSync/mkdirSync on arbitrary paths chosen by the server, returning file contents up to 10 MB over the socket. An UPGRADE message causes the client to run `npm install -g newtun@<server-chosen-version>` and respawn, letting the server push arbitrary future package versions. Every 5 seconds the client also beacons CPU, memory, network RX/TX, uptime, load, hostname, OS/arch/node version, and all non-internal IPv4 addresses to the same host, and on first run silently POSTs to /api/cli/service/install on that server. The remote endpoint is hardcoded rather than caller-supplied by default, and the shell/file/exec/upgrade channels give the server persistent RCE, arbitrary file read/write, and code-push over any host running the CLI.
